messages:
incident-bot: Pager triggered: private-vpc cluster 'orchid-prod' GPU pool reported sustained saturation >95% for 7m. queue_length=1240, oldest_request_ms=187000, capacity_left=0. Reason: autoscaler failing to add nodes.

alice (oncall): seeing the alert. i'm on it — grabbing context from dashboards.

monitoring-bot: CPU/GPU metrics: gpu_util 98%, pod_pending 312, node_boot_time median 8m (imagepull waits), scale_events suppressed (max_nodes=16) — policy cap hit.

ben (eng-runtime): @alice thanks. quick Q: is this the customer that set max_nodes=16 in their private deployment? that would explain the cap.

carla (infra-sre): confirmed — the cluster has max_nodes=16 and current nodes=16. autoscaler requests to cloud provider are returning 202 accepted but nodes stay NotReady due to imagepull backoff for custom app-image.

devon (support): FYI customer (Orchid Inc) is on call window. i've opened a support ticket and pinged their cust-eng.

frank (cust-eng): on the line — our image registry is healthy, but our custom init container pulls a ~10GB model shard from internal s3. recent network hiccup to the registry made image pulls time out.

eve (customer-ops): we are seeing realtime 503s for a fraction of routed requests ~1.8k/min, customers complaining. SLA window breached for their p95 latency.

alice (oncall): immediate mitigations: 1) enable fallback routing to hosted model for new requests, 2) scale down request concurrency to reduce queue growth, 3) try manual node restart if any NotReady nodes stuck in ImagePullBackOff.

ben (eng-runtime): how to enable fallback quickly? can we flip routing policy for this tenant?

carla (infra-sre): yes. we have a per-tenant routing override. command (console):
```
POST /v1/admin/routing-overrides
{ "tenant": "orchid-prod", "route": "hosted-fallback", "ttl": 3600 }
```
will route new traffic to hosted models. i can apply it in 60s.

devon (support): deploy request sent to ops-console. pinging @frank to confirm customer allows routed traffic to hosted.

frank (cust-eng): confirm — safe to route to hosted fallback for 30m while we resolve boot. go ahead.

alice (oncall): carla please apply override. also reduce per-tenant concurrency to 2 to reduce inflight tokens:
```
PATCH /v1/tenants/orchid-prod/config
{ "max_concurrency": 2 }
```

carla (infra-sre): applied routing override and reduced concurrency. monitoring shows immediate drop in new queued requests. queue_length now 890. older requests still pending.

monitoring-bot: queue_length: 890 -> 640 over 3m after override. p95 latency reduced from 14s -> 6.2s. some customer requests still erroring due to in-flight failures.

ben (eng-runtime): good. next: investigate why nodes stuck in ImagePullBackOff — logs show our init container `model-fetcher` retries failing with TLS: x509 certificate signed by unknown authority.

frank (cust-eng): that sounds like our internal registry rotated intermediate certs this morning. builders didn't update nodes' trusted CA bundle. we're on it.

carla (infra-sre): until certs are fixed, new nodes will fail bootstrap. two options: 1) temporarily relax node auto-registration health checks to allow node join then run a post-join init to fetch model shards (risky), 2) coordinate with customer to push CA bundle update to their registry config (safer).

alice (oncall): prefer option 2. coordinate with customer ENG to push CA update. @frank what's ETA?

frank (cust-eng): we can roll CA update in ~18 minutes. we will stage to a small batch first.

devon (support): informing customer success and the account owner. adding note to ticket: routed traffic to hosted fallback, limited concurrency, ongoing node bootstrap block due to cert rotation.

ben (eng-runtime): while waiting, can we free up capacity by evicting non-critical internal dev pools that are consuming GPUs in the same private cloud region?

carla (infra-sre): there are 3 dev pools with 6 gpus each but they belong to other tenant segments. we can request preemption; need approval from platform-schedule. i'll raise a preempt request.

carla (infra-sre): preempt request approved. draining 2 dev pools now. expected freed GPUs: 12.

monitoring-bot: after preempt: gpu_free_count +12, queue_length 640 -> 420 in 4m. some pending pods scheduled to freed nodes but still NotReady until CA fix.

alice (oncall): update for postmortem: root cause = customer registry cert rotation + tenant max_nodes cap prevented autoscaler from adding compensatory nodes. contributing factors: large model-shard init container (10GB) increased bootstrap time; no early fallback routing for private tenants.

devon (support): customer impact summary for the ticket: 503s experienced by ~2.5k requests over 22 minutes, p95 latency SLO breached during window, routed ~70% of new traffic to hosted fallback, no data leak. customer accepted temporary routing.

frank (cust-eng): CA rollout in progress. first 3 nodes successfully joined after bundle update. we see image pulls succeeding now.

monitoring-bot: nodes_notready count -> 0, scheduled_pods moving to Running. queue_length 420 -> 40 over 6m. p95 latency back to baseline ~120ms.

alice (oncall): good recovery. handing off to night oncall @ben for follow-up and postmortem. please capture timeline, mitigations, and action items.

ben (eng-runtime): taking handoff. action items I will own: 1) propose per-tenant early-fallback policy (configurable threshold), 2) add autoscaler alert when scale_request is accepted but nodes remain NotReady >5m, 3) docs for customer registry CA rotations and recommended bootstrapping patterns (avoid huge model pulls in init).

devon (support): i'll draft the customer-facing incident summary and share with account owner before 0900.

incident-bot: Incident resolved. Severity: P2 (customer impact, mitigated by fallback). Duration: 38m. Started: 2359876543, Resolved: 2359876607. Linked ticket: #INC-2026-0143.

ben (eng-runtime): will schedule postmortem sync tomorrow 09:30 PT. tagging @carla @devon @frank @alice.

frank (cust-eng): thanks for the rapid response. we'll follow up with registry cert rotation postmortem from our side.

alice (oncall): closing channel, handoff complete. :white_check_mark:
